question: Where are sales reps' monthly quotas kept, and how does the rep sales report pull out the right month's figure?

must_mention.note: quota lives in the MonthQuota field on the SalesRep table
MonthQuota is a 12-element extent array (Jan-Dec)
the report subscripts the array by the input month (MonthQuota[ip-month])

notes: db/ordermgmt.df lines 497-506: MonthQuota decimal EXTENT 12 on SalesRep. rpt/rpt-repsales.p line 38: d-quota = SalesRep.MonthQuota[ip-month].

question: The rep sales monthly report gets slow as invoice history grows - is there an indexing problem in how it selects the records?

must_mention.note: MONTH()/YEAR() functions wrap the date in the WHERE clause
that keeps the InvoiceDate index from bracketing (the index can't be used for a range read)
so it walks every ArHist row per rep

notes: rpt/rpt-repsales.p lines 7-9 (TODO comment) and 31-34: MONTH(ArHist.InvoiceDate)/YEAR(...) in the WHERE prevent InvoiceDate index bracketing; comment says it walks every ArHist row per rep. [must_mention tightened 2026-07-19 after an independent corpus audit: the old fact-2/3 matchers accepted the bare tokens InvoiceDate/ArHist, which a non-diagnostic or wrong answer also contains; fact 2 now requires the index-defeat idiom and fact 3 a scan description.]

question: Which program invokes deallocate-item in the allocation manager, and for which order lines does it get called?

must_mention.note: only oe-cancel.p calls it
invoked IN the persistent procedure handle gh-alloc
only for lines still in Ordered status; backordered lines were never allocated

notes: oe/oe-cancel.p lines 28-38: RUN inv/inv-alloc.p PERSISTENT SET gh-alloc; RUN deallocate-item IN gh-alloc only IF OrderLineStatus = {&LIN-ORDERED}. Header comment lines 9-10: backordered lines never allocated. No other caller in corpus.

question: Can individual installations hook their own custom logic into the nightly order posting run, and how does that mechanism work?

must_mention.note: the hook program is oe/oe-exit.p
run dynamically via RUN VALUE(), guarded by a SEARCH() check for the file
deliberately not in source control - each site drops its own copy on the PROPATH

notes: oe/oe-post.p lines 22, 95-98: c-exit-proc = 'oe/oe-exit.p'; IF SEARCH(c-exit-proc) <> ? THEN RUN VALUE(c-exit-proc); comment: deliberately NOT in source control, each site drops its own oe/oe-exit.p on the PROPATH.

question: I ran ship confirmation on an order, but the header is still Ordered - what can leave it that way?

must_mention.note: backordered lines are not shipped and hold the order open
ship-line skips a line when the Item record is locked (or missing), leaving it in Ordered status
the header only flips to Shipped when a CAN-FIND check finds no Ordered/Backordered lines left

notes: oe/oe-ship.p: lines 35-41 CAN-FIND for any line Ordered or Backordered gates the header status flip; ship-line lines 56-69 skips locked or missing Item and RETURNs, leaving the line Ordered; header comment lines 10-11 says backordered lines hold the order open.

question: When the nightly post runs, does it also relieve inventory for the orders it posts?

must_mention.note: no - inventory relief was moved out to oe-ship.p (ship confirmation) in 2007
the old relief code in oe-post.p survives only as a comment kept for reference

notes: oe/oe-post.p lines 8-10 (history: inventory relief moved OUT to oe-ship.p 04/2007) and lines 84-90: the OnHand/Allocated decrement block is commented out ('kept for reference, dm'). Live relief is oe/oe-ship.p ship-line lines 71-73.

question: After an order line is created, which procedures can later change its line status, and what values do they set?

must_mention.note: ship confirmation (oe-ship.p ship-line) is one writer
order cancellation (oe-cancel.p) is the other writer
the values written are Shipped and Cancelled

notes: OrderLine.OrderLineStatus is assigned after creation only in oe/oe-ship.p ship-line (line 73, {&LIN-SHIPPED}) and oe/oe-cancel.p main (line 40, {&LIN-CANCELLED}). oe-entry.p add-order-line sets the initial value; oe-post.p only reads line status.

question: If a customer is only slightly over their credit limit, will order entry still decline the order?

must_mention.note: there is a tolerance of 100 above the limit before declining
the check compares AR balance plus open-order exposure against CreditLimit plus the tolerance

notes: oe/oe-credit.p line 21: d-tolerance DECIMAL INITIAL 100 (added 10/2009 per header history); check-credit lines 61-62: declines only when sb-cust.Balance + get-open-balance() > sb-cust.CreditLimit + d-tolerance.
